Articulation Agreement Overview

This agreement outlines lower-division course requirements specific to the major. Students are strongly encouraged to consult an academic advisor to ensure they meet all degree requirements for their intended baccalaureate program.


Helpful Resources:

  • CSUB Catalog
  • Transfer Admission Requirements
  • Academic Advising Student Centers
  • CSUB Program Pathways Mapper


Course Equivalency Information for 4-Year Institutions

Students and staff can explore course transfer equivalencies through the Transfer Evaluation System (TES). Equivalency agreements are updated regularly and subject to change. For the most current information, please refer to TES or contact the Articulation Office.

","groupId":"212e6645-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"About the Major","groupId":"232e6645-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":2,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

The Bachelor of Science Degree in Kinesiology at CSUB covers a broad knowledge base that represents several disciplines that include physical activity leadership, clinical exercise science, personal training and allied health professions. Students majoring in Kinesiology have three concentrations to choose from: Applied Exercise Science, Physical Activity Leadership and Allied Health.


The Kinesiology department also offers a minor in Kinesiology and a variety of activity courses that provide recreation and fitness opportunities for all CSUB students.


For additional information, visit the following:

Department of Kinesiology

Program Requirements - Kinesiology, BS, Concentration in Applied Exercise Science
